Subject: Post-call: OmniHealth data handling options & next steps

Hi Sam / Jenna —

Great to meet today — appreciate you walking us through the use cases and the PHI constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we scope a pilot: 

Summary of constraints we heard on the call:
- PHI must never be retained beyond the endpoint (customer requires 0-retention for any payloads flagged as PHI).
- Aggregated/debug logs can be retained for short windows for troubleshooting; OmniHealth prefer 7 days as a maximum.
- Data residency: EU for EU patients; US for US patients.
- Access controls: strict role-based access to any logs, and SOC2 evidence for controls required.

Two near-term options we propose for a pilot:
A) Zero-retention mode for PHI traffic: ephemeral processing, no write-to-disk, K/V cache disabled for those sessions. This preserves latency but reduces caching benefits.
B) Short retention + redaction: redact PII at ingress, store sanitized debug logs for 7 days, full audit trail in restricted storage (accessed only by your security team).

Can you confirm which option you prefer for the initial pilot (A or B), or if you want a hybrid (PHI = A, non-PHI = B)? Once you confirm, we'll bring in engineering to scope the configuration and provide pricing delta.

Attached: post-call notes and a draft retention schedule we can iterate on.

Next steps suggested:
- You confirm A/B/hybrid by end of week.
- We produce a short technical note (Karthik) + SOW that shows the dataflow and per-tenant settings.
- Security exchange: you send the minimum evidence list you need (SOC2 report, pen test summary), we'll attach our compliance pack and set up an evidence share.

Thanks — Evelyn

Subject: Re: OmniHealth retention ask — feasibility notes

Hi all — quick technical note on feasibility and tradeoffs. TL;DR: Yes, we can support per-tenant retention and a true 0-retention mode, with caveats and a modest pricing delta.

Details:
- Per-tenant retention: We can apply retention metadata at routing time. Policy layer supports per-tenant overrides so logs and debug events can follow an attached retention TTL. We would implement this as a per-route policy in the control plane.
- Zero-retention for PHI: Implementable by turning off write-ahead logs for matched traffic, disabling KV cache writes, and ensuring in-memory-only model session handling. Backend changes required: a runtime flag per model-variant to avoid any persistence path. We also need to disable async analytics export for those sessions.
- PII redaction: We recommend ingress-level deterministic redaction for common PHI patterns + optional customer-provided regex/es. This reduces risk but is not a substitute for the 0-retention mode if regulation requires absolutely no persistence.

Tradeoffs / implications:
- Latency: Zero-retention removes caching benefits; expect a marginal latency increase (median +20-40ms) for affected traffic.
- Cost: Because of reduced batching and cache hit degradation, zero-retention will increase per-request cost. Ballpark: 8-12% uplift on inference run rate for that traffic; additional eng hours for SRE to instrument.
- Observability: Debugging is harder for zero-retention traffic; we recommend a short-term debug window (ephemeral internal trace IDs) that expire immediately after triage and are scoped to specific SRE users.

Required items to proceed:
1) Signed pilot SOW that enumerates volumes and SLA for the pilot.
2) OmniHealth to flag PHI traffic at ingress (header or payload flag).
3) Agreement on retention TTLs and access roles for redacted logs.

I attached a short implementation note and a config snippet for the per-tenant retention policy. Happy to walk through with your infra/security team.

Thanks — Karthik

Pilot outline:
- Scope: PHI-marked sessions in zero-retention mode (per-tenant toggle) for up to 500k tokens/day + non-PHI traffic with redacted 7-day logs.
- Duration: 6 weeks.
- Price: No uplift for the 7-day redacted logs. For zero-retention traffic we propose a +10% per-token surcharge to cover the reduced caching efficiency and SRE support.
- Deliverables: technical runbook, per-tenant retention configs, SOC2 snapshot and pen test summary (redwood to provide).
- Success criteria: latency within agreed bounds (+50ms abs), no persistent storage of PHI, and ability to retrieve redacted logs within 7 days.
